title: Measurements of isolated photon pair production in association with jets in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 8 TeV with the ATLAS detector
comment: 56 pages in total, author list starting page 39, 17 figures, 4 tables, submitted to Phys. Rev. D. All figures including auxiliary figures are available at https://atlas.web.cern.ch/Atlas/GROUPS/PHYSICS/PAPERS/STDM-2016-12/
summary: Measurements of integrated and differential production cross section of two isolated photons in events with and without associated hadronic jets based on the 2012 dataset of 20.3 fb$^{-1}$ integrated luminosity of proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}=8$ TeV collected by the ATLAS experiment are presented. The measurements consider photons with pseudorapidities of $|η^γ|<1.37$ or $1.56<|η^γ|<2.37$ and transverse energy of $E_{T}^γ>22$ GeV. Jets are required to have $p_{T}^{j}>25$ GeV for $|η^{j}|<2.4$ and $p_{T}^{j}>50$ GeV for $2.4<|η^{j}|<4.4$. Events are classified into categories based on the number of jets and integrated fiducial cross sections of diphoton production in association with inclusive and exclusive number of jets are presented. Fiducial cross sections, differential in sixteen diphoton, jet, dijet and photon-jet observables, are presented and compared with leading-order Sherpa 1.4.1 predictions in all jet categories, fixed-order next-to-leading-order GoSam and BlackHat calculations in selected categories, and NLO-matched predictions from Sherpa 2.2.14 in all categories. Overall, the NLO predictions provide a reasonable description of the data, with significant discrepancies observed for increasing jet multiplicity, particularly for angular variables, attributable to the absence of higher-order terms in the calculations. The Sherpa 2.2.14 NLO-matched predictions provide the best overall description of the data across all jet categories and observables.

title: Operational Challenges in Efficient and Sustainable Operation of the Event Processing Nodes GPU Farm at the ALICE Experiment
summary: ALICE's Event Processing Nodes (EPN) farm is CERN's largest GPU computing facility by capacity, comprising 350 GPU-based nodes and 2800 GPUs delivering approximately a total of 48\,PFLOP/s. It has successfully enabled real-time processing of heavy-ion collisions at 50\,kHz during LHC Run~3. The facility was designed for sustainability, extended hardware lifetime, and reduced operational overhead. High availability is supported by a robust technical architecture and well-defined operational practices, ensuring reliable and continuous operation throughout data taking.

title: Photon-Counting Readout via Electro-Optic Microwave-to-Optical Transduction for Axion Haloscopes
summary: Axion dark matter searches require highly sensitive detection schemes with high scan rate to efficiently explore the parameter space. Building upon the conventional Sikivie haloscope, where axions convert into microwave photons inside a magnetic-field-immersed resonant cavity, we present a photon-counting scheme based on an electro-optic microwave-to-optical transducer. Through a comprehensive theoretical model under realistic experimental constraints, we find that the optimal operating regime employs an overcoupled microwave cavity, trading peak transduction efficiency for reduced transducer noise. Furthermore, combining parameters already demonstrated in existing devices, in a device with optimized extrinsic coupling rates, would yield a scan-rate enhancement of 5-10 relative to quantum-limited homodyne detection. Improvements in quality factors, coupling rates, and thermal management push this enhancement beyond 50. While our quantitative model is benchmarked at 9 GHz, the scheme adapts well to haloscopes across the 5-12 GHz range, where shrinking cavity volumes severely degrade the achievable scan rate. These results demonstrate the potential of electro-optical photon detection as a high-speed detection technique for axion dark matter searches.

title: The Search for the Top Quark
comment: 15 pages, 4 figures, Proceedings of the 4th International Symposium on the History of Particle Physics, CERN, November 2025
summary: The discovery of the top quark in 1995 completed the roster of the matter particles, quarks and leptons, expected in the Standard Model and in many of its suggested extensions. However, the top quark does not conform to the pattern set by its sister quarks and has come to be a critical component of the ongoing searches for physics beyond the prevailing paradigm. (Prepared for the Proceedings of the 4th International Symposium on the History of Particle Physics, CERN, Nov. 2025.)

title: Representation theory and massive spectral zeta functions on spherical space forms
comment: 64 pages plus appendices, in preparation for submission to the Journal of Mathematical Physics
summary:
We study the spectral theory of the massive scalar kinetic operator on spherical space forms $Γ\backslash S^{3}$, where $Γ$ is a finite subgroup of $\mathrm{SO}(4)$ acting freely on $S^{3}$. Using the Peter-Weyl theorem and Molien series we compute the spectrum of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on $Γ\backslash S^3$ directly from representation theory, obtaining the eigenvalues and their multiplicities for all lens spaces $L(p,q)$ and for each ADE-class of finite subgroups of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, which includes homogeneous lens spaces, prism spaces and quotients by the binary tetrahedral, octahedral and icosahedral groups, the last also known as the Poincaré homology sphere.
  For homogeneous quotients by subgroups of even order, we construct the meromorphic continuation of the spectral zeta function of the massive kinetic operator and obtain the general zeta-regularized determinant in closed form. The determinant is expressed as a finite sum of polylogarithms, valid for all real mass, and depends on $Γ$ only through its order and a finite set of parameters which we call twist coefficients fixed by the dimensions of the $Γ$-invariant subspaces.
  As a complementary approach, we express the heat trace of the kinetic operator on spherical space forms in terms of Jacobi theta functions, whose modular properties relate the spectral zeta function to geometric data, the volume and closed geodesic lengths of $Γ\backslash S^3$. We find that the spectral zeta function admits a rapidly convergent expansion in the heavy mass sector in terms of modified Bessel functions, and provides an independent check on the determinant.
  This framework extends to quotients of higher-dimensional manifolds directly, which we outline for future work.

title: The Start Time of Ringdown
summary: We determine the convergence of quasi-normal modes sums for a point-particle plunging into a Schwarzschild black hole. While a dynamical amplitude model reproduces the waveform after the particle crosses the bounce radius, a constant amplitude sum converges only after the start time $t_S$, which corresponds to the advanced time at which the particle hits the central singularity. For a plunge from the ISCO, $t_S \simeq 9.4 M$ after the peak of the $22$ mode. After $t_S$, dynamical and constant amplitudes models are equivalent; our analysis also implies that any "direct wave" must reduce to the late-time tail after $t_S$.

title: Exact thermal correlators at vanishing momenta and the black hole singularity
summary: We study thermal two- and three-point functions of scalar primaries in holographic CFTs dual to AdS black branes. The three-point function arises from a cubic scalar interaction in the bulk. At vanishing external momenta, the tree-level results can be written in closed form and are exact in the operator dimensions. We reproduce them through direct CFT calculations in two dimensions. Their large-dimension expansions contain subleading exponential terms encoding the radial proper time from the horizon to the black hole singularity. These results provide an exact test of earlier WKB and saddle-point predictions for higher-point thermal correlators, confirming the proper-time signature while correcting the predicted asymptotic form.

title: Shapiro spikes in driven quantum fluids
summary: Periodic driving of a Josephson junction produces resonant transport signatures known as Shapiro spikes, conventionally described by effective circuit models. Here, we demonstrate Shapiro spikes in a neutral quantum fluid using simulations of a potential-biased atomic Josephson junction. The dc-current resonances follow the expected Bessel-function scaling, including the suppression and revival of individual resonances with increasing modulation strength. We uncover their microscopic mechanism by showing that the phase-winding frequency develops finite plateaus at integer multiples of the drive frequency. These phase-locked states are sustained by quantized-vortex nucleation and the associated $2π$ phase slips. Remarkably, within a locking plateau, the dc current and density transfer can reverse direction while the phase-winding frequency remains locked to the drive, giving rise to negative-mobility transport. Our results establish a microscopic link between vortex-mediated phase slips, Shapiro resonances, and anomalous transport in a neutral quantum fluid, revealing how quantized vortices convert resonant transport into phase-locked dynamics with negative mobility.

title: Top Spin and CP from Equivariant Transformers
summary: Measurements of spin correlations and CP are an exciting and challenging part of the precision-LHC program. We first show how L-GATr-slim, as a Lorentz-equivariant transformer, significantly boosts the spin analyzing power for hadronic top quarks. We then show how adding a pseudoscalar channel to its architecture allows us to learn and interpret optimal observables and their CP properties. We demonstrate this for WBF-Higgs production at parton level and top pair production including detector effects.

title: Rough-to-frozen transition in non-integrable dimer models
summary: The transition from rough to frozen phases in models of random surfaces is expected to be governed by the Pokrovsky-Talapov law, which predicts a $\varepsilon^{3/2}$-type singularity of the macroscopic height profile (limit shape), as the distance $\varepsilon$ from the frozen phase (facet) is sent to zero. This has been proved so far only in exactly solvable cases, notably the classical, determinantal, 2D dimer model. In this paper we prove the validity of the Pokrovsky-Talapov law for a non-integrable 2D dimer model on the hexagonal lattice, whose Gibbs weight depends upon a weak plaquette interaction among dimers. Our proof is based on a multiscale analysis (constructive fermionic Renormalization Group), which allows us to identify two different regimes with distinct scaling properties and to explain the universality of the Pokrovsky-Talapov exponent $3/2$, in contrast with the interaction-dependent critical exponents characterizing the rough phase. The first regime, corresponding to smaller distances, is characterized by an effective quadratic dispersion relation, while the second comes with an effective linear dispersion relation, typical of Luttinger liquid behavior. As a byproduct of our construction, we control the scaling limit of the interacting dimer model uniformly in the distance from the frozen phase.

title: The quasi-topological space of quasi-topological gravities
summary: We investigate general properties of quasi-topological theories of gravity involving infinite towers of polynomial densities and of their regular vacuum black hole solutions. We show that every positive-mass regular vacuum solution necessarily possesses a de Sitter core, while Minkowski and anti-de Sitter cores are excluded. Regarding the horizon structure, we prove that asymptotically flat and anti-de Sitter regular black holes always admit extremal configurations. We find that there is no upper bound on the number of horizons and that horizons of arbitrarily high degeneracy can arise. These results extend to more general theories of gravity with second-order equations on spherically symmetric backgrounds. Finally, we characterize the space of quasi-topological theories admitting regular black holes, showing that it is contractible (in particular, path-connected and simply connected) and that regularity is stable under suitably small deformations of the higher-order couplings. In the sense of Spanier, this space is naturally a contractible \emph{quasi-topological} space. Additionally, we prove that any theory defined by a set of couplings up to any arbitrarily high, but finite, curvature order can be completed into a theory yielding regular black hole solutions, while preserving the same set of lower-order couplings. These results show that regular solutions arise in a broad class of quasi-topological gravities and do not require fine-tuning of the couplings.

title: Satisfying Freed--Witten quantization on smooth divisors in Calabi--Yau orientifolds
comment: 8+4 pages of main text and appendices
summary: Freed--Witten quantization conditions on several divisors wrapped by D-branes must be satisfied with one bulk $B$-field. On a smooth Calabi--Yau threefold $X$ with a holomorphic O3/O7 involution $σ$, we show that the common background $B_{2,+}^{\star}=\tfrac12[R]$, where $R$ is the total O7 divisor, permits Freed--Witten period quantization on the full two-cycle lattice of \emph{every smooth connected divisor}, modulo torsion. The worldvolume fluxes are chosen individually and obey the orientifold relation between each divisor and its image. The central step concerns setwise invariant divisors $D$: we prove that the bulk Freed--Witten class $η_D^\star=\tfrac12([R]+[D])|_D$ has integer periods on every $σ$-even integral two-cycle class, including inherited and autochthonous classes. Its periods on purely $σ$-odd classes vanish, so any remaining non-integer periods occur only on classes that are neither $σ$-even nor $σ$-odd. We show how to choose $σ$-odd worldvolume fluxes on these invariant divisors that make all periods integral. For exchanged divisor pairs, quantizing the flux on one member automatically quantizes its orientifold image. On invariant divisors with $h^{2,0}_-(D)=0$, the constructed flux is of type $(1,1)$ and admits a primitive representative; this includes every smooth rigid invariant divisor. We also study zero worldvolume flux on invariant divisors. For $h^{1,1}_-(X)\leq1$, we construct common bulk backgrounds satisfying every inherited intersection period on all such divisors. A binary compatibility test determines whether a common shift exists for larger $h^{1,1}_-(X)$. Non-inherited period tests then determine whether the resulting backgrounds allow zero flux on the full worldvolume lattices.

title: Quasicrystals are Functionally Graded Materials
summary: Quasicrystals exhibit long-range order without translational periodicity, posing challenges to compute their electronic properties. Here we show that a quasicrystal can be represented exactly as a periodic approximant with a spatially graded phason, establishing a connection to functionally graded materials. Building on this connection, we develop a controlled quantum theory of quasicrystals. We derive a state-dependent control parameter governed by the quantum metric of local Bloch states, determining when finite approximations are reliable. We further construct a Hamiltonian that correctly predicts Bragg gap positions, quasimomentum equivalence, and quasiperiodic eigenstates to all orders in phason strain within a finite Fourier window. We verify the theory numerically and propose a diffraction-based experimental test of the gap shift induced by phason strain. Our framework opens a route to predicting the electronic structure and functional properties of quasicrystals using methods developed for functionally graded materials.

title: Indirect probes of heavy neutral leptons through the dipole portal at FCC-ee
summary: We study indirect probes of the gauge-invariant dipole portal of Majorana heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) at FCC-ee. Virtual HNLs modify electroweak gauge-boson propagation and lepton couplings through loops with two dipole interactions. We calculate the resulting finite matching corrections and their effects on $Z$-pole observables. For real, flavour-aligned couplings, the local response is specified by four combinations of coupling shifts. Independent local ultraviolet interactions can reproduce all four, making the dipole interpretation dependent on assumptions about those interactions. With improved Standard Model predictions, FCC-ee can probe equal, same-sign hypercharge and weak dipole coefficients as small as $0.14\,\mathrm{TeV}^{-2}$ at an HNL mass of 1 TeV. This projection assumes dipole dominance, with independent ultraviolet coefficients set to zero at twice the HNL mass. We quantify how additional ultraviolet contributions can weaken or strengthen the sensitivity. At 1 TeV, the projected reach is competitive with HL-LHC same-sign dilepton searches for Majorana HNLs, while larger masses allow smaller dipole coefficients to be probed within the effective theory's domain of validity. Radiative Higgs decays offer a modest further improvement. The FeynRules, FeynArts and UFO models used in this analysis are publicly available at \href{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23667622}{doi:10.5281/zenodo.23667622}.

title: Stroh--Hamiltonian Framework for Modeling Incompressible Poroelastic Materials
summary: The Stroh sextic formalism, developed by Stroh, offers a compelling framework for representing the equilibrium equations in anisotropic elasticity. This approach has proven particularly effective for studying multilayered structures and time-harmonic problems, owing to its ability to seamlessly integrate physical constraints into the analysis. By recognizing that the Stroh formalism aligns with the canonical Hamiltonian structure, this work extends its application to Biot's poroelasticity, focusing on scenarios where the solid material is incompressible and there is no fluid pressure gradient. The study introduces a novel Hamiltonian-based approach to analyze such systems, offering deeper insights into the interplay between solid incompressibility and fluid-solid coupling. A key novelty lies in the derivation of canonical equations under these constraints, enabling clearer interpretations of reversible poroelastic behavior. However, the framework assumes perfectly drained conditions and neglects dissipative effects, which limits its applicability to fully realistic scenarios involving energy loss or complex fluid dynamics. Despite this limitation, the work provides a foundational step toward understanding constrained poroelastic systems and paves the way for future extensions to more general cases, including dissipative and nonlinear regimes.

title: Black hole quasinormal mode excitation and mixing for coupled fields
summary: The idea of testing the nature of black holes and possible deviations from general relativity from their oscillation spectrum, known as ``black hole spectroscopy'', has become an experimental science. In many modified theories of gravity, the gravitational perturbations couple to additional degrees of freedom, leading to mode mixing and to a more complex ringdown signal. We adopt the parametrized quasinormal mode formalism for nonrotating black holes to study coupled perturbations in modified gravity theories in order to understand how the interaction with additional fields affects the quasinormal mode frequencies and their amplitudes. We compute the quasinormal mode spectrum of the coupled system in the frequency domain using direct integration and a matrix-valued continued-fraction method. We then compare the results with time-domain evolutions, where we extract the mode frequencies and amplitudes using the Prony method as well as least-squares fitting. In the weak-coupling regime, the scaling of the amplitudes associated with the gravitational-led and secondary-led modes can be understood perturbatively. The excitation of additional families of ringdown modes can become significant even when the frequency shifts remain moderate. We use our numerical time evolutions to provide ready-to-use coefficients for the mode amplitudes for representative initial data configurations. We work out specific examples, including dynamical Chern-Simons gravity and the special near-resonant case of coupled perturbations between the polar and axial quasinormal modes. Our theory-agnostic characterization of coupled systems should be useful to quantify systematic effects in black hole spectroscopy with next-generation gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Goldstone theory of gluon saturation in high energy QCD: From color glass to color superfluid condensate
summary: In the high energy Regge asymptotics of QCD, the rapid overpopulation of gluons leads to gluon saturation, characterized by nonperturbative semi-classical lumpy configurations of size $1/Q_S$, where $Q_S\gg Λ_{\rm QCD}$ is a dynamical semi-hard saturation scale. We discuss here a generalization of the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework describing this phenomenon that is obtained by carefully treating the breaking of global symmetries by the condensate. In particular, we show that the breaking of a global subgroup of color results in a Goldstone effective field theory (EFT) whose dynamics is characterized by a Goldstone decay constant $f_G = \sqrt{N} Q_S$, where $N=O(1/α_S)$ is the phase space occupancy of the condensate, which is large for $α_S(Q_S)\ll 1$. Further, the coupling of these colored Goldstones to collinear gluon modes leads to a depletion of the condensate, thereby modifying the static shockwave scattering framework of the CGC on timescales controlled by $f_G$. The CGC EFT on these longer time scales is a novel color superfluid. Low frequency modes with $ω\leq α_S Q_S$ in an external probe of the CGC are sensitive to superfluid dynamics, with interesting physical consequences for deeply inelastic scattering and ultrarelativistic nuclear collisions.

title: Resonantly interacting $2e/3$ anyons: a controlled microscopic theory of anyon superconductivity
summary: We develop a microscopic theory of anyon superconductivity that connects electronic interactions in a lightly doped Laughlin state to the universal physics of a resonantly interacting anyon gas. Using geometric quantization of Laughlin quasiholes, we derive the effective many-body Hamiltonian of dilute charge-$2e/3$ anyons, including their valley structure, dispersion, and statistical and short-range interactions, together with an explicit map between anyon and electron observables. This reduces the dilute many-body problem to a few parameters fixed by data computable from few anyon numerics. In analogy with resonant Fermi and Bose gases, we organize the dilute anyon problem around a two-body binding resonance and its relevant and marginal perturbations. For a three-valley gas of charge-$2e/3$ anyons, we identify a resonance whose long-distance theory is governed by an Aharonov-Casher anyon Hamiltonian whose magnetic field is the statistical Chern-Simons field and whose ground state is exactly solvable. Using the ground state wavefunction, we demonstrate Cooper-pair off-diagonal long-range order directly in electron coordinates and determine the pairing symmetry and vortex-lattice structure. The leading perturbations at the fixed point are a relevant pair detuning and a marginal three-body contact in the valley-singlet channel, which determine the compressibility and sound velocity. A repulsive three-body coupling is marginally irrelevant, allowing the fixed point to control a parametrically broad dilute regime near pair resonance, while attractive three-body interactions instead generate charge-$2e$ trimers. More broadly, our results show that binding thresholds between competing anyon composites host universal resonant regimes that are not captured by the lowest-energy anyon species alone, providing a new setting for controlled theories of anyon matter.

title: Proton generalized parton distributions from electromagnetic form factors: A theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction
summary: We present a theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction of the unpolarized, chiral-even, leading-twist proton generalized parton distributions $H^q$ and $E^q$. At zero skewness, valence-quark distributions are combined with flavor-dependent exponential profiles calibrated simultaneously against phenomenological representations of the proton and neutron electromagnetic form factors. The construction imposes exact valence and anomalous-magnetic-moment normalizations, the low-scale condition $B^{u+d}(0)=0$, the required endpoint behavior, and the complete Gaussian impact-parameter positivity bound. The resulting parametrization provides a reasonable description of the electromagnetic form factors and their slopes while revealing the tension between strict GPD consistency and a precision reproduction of all low-$Q^2$ observables within the adopted ansatz. We extend the distributions to nonzero skewness using normalized double distributions and introduce an independent $D$-term to complete the relevant Mellin polynomials. We examine electromagnetic and energy--momentum-tensor form factors, impact-parameter distributions, positivity, polynomiality, and illustrative mechanical properties. The analysis distinguishes information constrained by electromagnetic data from additional assumptions governing skewness and the mechanical sector, thereby providing a transparent elastic baseline for future studies of nucleon-to-resonance transition GPDs.

title: When light travels with infinite speed: the electromagnetic loop circuits
summary: Considering the ideal limit where the speed of light is infinite, or more precisely where the permittivity and permeability of the vaccuum are both zero, we construct a new type of electromagnetic circuit that we name an EM-loop circuit. These consist of wires having very high permittivity (E-wires) and wires having very high permeability (M-wires). These are threaded together by coils, the E-wire loops and M-wire loops. Some of the loops are terminal loops, pierced by an applied magnetic flux (for E-wire loops) or an applied displacement field (for M-wire loops) that are outside the vacuum since it does not support these fields. The response is the net flux of displacement field through a cross section of each E-wire terminal loop and the net magnetic flux through a cross section of each terminal M-wire loop. To calculate this response, the fields at the internal loops (those that are not terminal loops) are eliminated from the equations.It turns out that the response is governed by a new class of function pairs - dual Herglotz functions. Superpositions of a special class of EM-loop circuits, termed fundamental, allow us to realize any pair of dual Herglotz functions. Thus, we have obtained a complete characterization of the response functions of EM-loop circuits.

title: Geodesic completeness and photon propagation in a superconducting T-duality black hole
comment: 17 pages, no figures. Comments are welcome
summary: The purpose of this article is twofold. First, we study the geodesic completeness of the string T-duality black hole with the Raychaudhuri equation, for radial massive particles of arbitrary specific energy $\varepsilon$. Exact proper-time quadratures reveal three classes of observers: supercritical observers reach the regular centre in finite proper time through a caustic and pass through it, critical observers ($\varepsilon=1$) approach it only asymptotically with finite expansion, and subcritical observers are reflected at a fold caustic. Because the lapse is analytic and even in $r$, geodesics continue regularly through the centre, and all three classes are complete on the stipulated maximal extension. A diverging expansion therefore signals a caustic of the congruence rather than an endpoint of the geodesics, in contrast with Schwarzschild spacetime. Second, radial Maxwell rays are likewise complete but form a single class, since a massless ray carries no energy scale. We propose to model the black-hole core itself as a superconductor, with London response $μ^2=4πκρ$ attributed to the existing source. A symmetry-breaking potential with a vacuum-energy offset reproduces the de Sitter core and its photon mass exactly at the centre and approximately in the inner core; since no static scalar theory reproduces the anisotropic source further out, the full radial response remains phenomenological. The resulting Hamiltonian rays follow timelike geodesics of $μ^2g_{μν}$ up to reparametrisation and reproduce the three classes, separated by the central mass $μ_0$, while the density gradient of the core adds a defocusing contribution near the centre. We also distinguish Hamiltonian completeness from completeness of the conformal metric.

title: Schwinger Effect with a Transversal Boundary
summary: We study the effect of a boundary on pair production by an electric field. In particular, we are interested in the case in which the electric field has a normal component with respect to the boundary. This is essentially more complex than pure tangential fields due to the reflection of created particles against the boundary. In this article we provide the explicit solution for the case of an instantaneous electric pulse which is spatially uniform and normal to a flat surface. We show that pair production exhibits a bulk contribution that accounts for the interference of reflected modes, in addition to a purely boundary term. To conclude, we give an expression for the total particle production due to an irrotational electric pulse in a region delimited by an arbitrary boundary.

title: Classification and Signatures of Dissipative Quantum Hall-Superconductor Junctions
summary: Fractional quantum Hall (FQH) edges with proximity-induced superconductivity can host parafermionic zero modes (PZMs), making them a promising platform for topological quantum computing. Recent experiments [Gül et al., Phys. Rev. X 12, 021057 (2022)] measured the edge conductance from crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) between counter-propagating FQH edges separated by a narrow superconductor. The observed conductance was small and non-quantized, with two distinct behaviors: some states show temperature-independent conductance, while others show conductance that grows as temperature decreases. We explain these results by dissipation to sub-gap modes in the superconductor and present a phase diagram for the FQH-superconductor junction. We show that for Jain states, temperature-independent non-quantized conductance occurs only in the presence of an integer mode (such as at filling $ν=1\pm\frac{1}{m}$, with odd $m\geq3$) strongly coupled to the dissipative channel. The predicted temperature trends qualitatively agree with the experiment, which shows temperature-independent conductance for $ν=2/3$ and integer states, but not for $ν=1/3$ and $ν=2/5$. We propose comparing $ν=4/3$ and $2/3$ to test the predicted influence of the relative chirality of integer and fractional modes.

title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
summary: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. We characterize aspects of the amplifier performance relevant to axion searches, including gain drift, compression point, amplifier noise at various operating temperatures, readout with an input circulator, and magnetic field insensitivity.

title: A liquid vapor phase transition in quantum statistical mechanics
summary: We prove a liquid vapor phase transition for a quantum system of particles in the continuum. The system is the quantum version with Boltzmann statistics of the point particles model introduced in by Lebowitz, Mazel and Presutti.

title: Bumblebee radiation from neutral matter around a black hole
comment: 12 pages in double column and 5 figures
summary: We investigate bumblebee radiation generated by neutral matter orbiting a black hole with a radial spacelike vector vacuum. Starting from a point particle coupled minimally to the metric, we derive the curvature induced vector current and the potential response required by its conservation. For a localized circular source with no independent radial boundary current, this response gives $δV'=ξρ/4$. The axial vector source instead follows the radial transport of angular momentum and vanishes for circular motion. A slightly eccentric orbit excites an axial dipole at the orbital frequency $Ω$ and a quadrupole contribution at $2Ω$, with outgoing amplitudes proportional to $ev^3$ and $ev^4$, respectively, where $v=\sqrt{M/a}$. We construct their retarded response and obtain the leading coefficients through weak field matching. Reconstruction of the observer's tidal tensor gives the dipole strain $h_{\hat r\hatφ}^{V,10}=ξ^2b^2μev^3\sinθ\cos[Ω(t-R)]/(8πR)$. The corresponding partial luminosity is $P_{B,10}^{\infty}=ξ^2b^2μ^2e^2v^{12}/(48πM^2)$ at the leading order. Remarkably, the ordinary neutral matter produces an additional radial transverse tidal signal even when the homogeneous gravitational master operator remains in Schwarzschild form.

title: Complex phase diagram and thermodynamic supercriticality of five-dimensional four-charge AdS black holes in $STU-W^2U$ gauged supergravity
summary: In this paper, we investigate the complex phase structure and thermodynamic supercriticality of static four-charge anti-de Sitter (AdS) black holes in five-dimensional $STU-W^2U$ gauged supergravity, with all four physical electric charges held fixed. A Van der Waals-like first-order small/large black hole phase transition is found to terminate at a critical point. By analytically continuing the fixed-charge thermodynamic relations, we trace the two real spinodal singularities through criticality into a complex-conjugate pair in the supercritical region. The corresponding spinodal temperatures exhibit the characteristic $3/2$ near-critical scaling, connecting the subcritical temperature splitting with the imaginary parts of the supercritical complex temperatures. We construct the associated complex phase diagram and identify a Widom-type crossover line from the real-temperature projection of the complex spinodals. This line progressively deviates from the locus of real heat-capacity maxima as the pressure increases. At higher pressures, the real heat-capacity extrema eventually merge and disappear, while the complex spinodal singularities persist. Together, these results reveal a continuous connection between critical phase transitions and supercritical thermodynamics through complex singularity structures, providing further insight into the thermodynamic phase behavior of multicharge supergravity black holes.

title: Bypass Transition via the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect
summary: Non-Hermitian skin lattices can directionally amplify propagating signals. Here we show that this amplification and nonlinear feedback together drive a bypass transition to self-sustained motion, familiar from shear flows. A finite local excitation can trigger sustained periodic or chaotic motion while the resting state remains linearly stable. We develop a return-map theory that predicts the triggering threshold, its scaling with directional gain, and the instability governing near-critical dynamics. The threshold decreases exponentially with chain length. Weak noise triggers sustained motion as well, with a characteristic ignition length that grows logarithmically as noise weakens at fixed observation time. Our work establishes a skin-effect route to bypass transitions, opening a new avenue for predicting and controlling nonlinear wave dynamics.

title: Born spreading with consistent shower starting scales in MC@NLO and FxFx merging
summary: Negative weights are a major cost in NLO event generation matched to parton showers at the LHC, as they increase the number of events needed for a given statistical precision. Born spreading reduces the fraction of negative-weight $\mathbb S$ events in MC@NLO by redistributing the Born contribution over the radiation variables. It introduces no bias only if everything that is passed to the parton shower together with $\mathbb S$ events depends on Born-level quantities alone. We show that the same condition is needed for the MC counterterms to reproduce the first shower emission, independently of how the radiation phase space is integrated. In MadGraph5_aMC@NLO, the $\mathbb S$-event starting scales did not fully satisfy this condition, which so far prevented the public release of Born spreading. We present a new and consistent construction of the starting scales for ordinary MC@NLO, FxFx merging and MC@NLO-$Δ$, with which Born spreading is now publicly available, including for merged samples. We also study modified formulations of the MC counterterms, and FxFx-merged $W$+jets production with up to two jets at NLO, for which Born spreading reduces the fraction of negative weights after merging without affecting the predictions, and the event samples are generated six times faster than with the former implementation.

title: Dynamical Signatures of Selective Gap Closing in Multi-Dimensional Monotone Quasiperiodic Operators
summary: We translate the spectral gap-closing criterion for multi-dimensional monotone quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators into a concrete dynamical protocol and verify it by large-scale numerics. For a non-principal label we construct a sampling function whose leading eigenfunction weight at the origin vanishes; a local bump then drives the residual weight through zero. The height of a weighted oscillatory time average of the origin-to-localization-center correlator exhibits a deep minimum precisely at the closing, while the site-control label remains featureless and orders of magnitude larger. The signature is robust and maps directly onto superconducting-circuit and photonic platforms.

title: Exact teleportation bounds for fermionic Hawking thermality beyond the single-mode approximation
summary: Fermionic teleportation near a Schwarzschild horizon involves two physically distinct ingredients that are often varied together: Hawking thermal mixing and the relative composition of the right and left Unruh modes. We separate them by factorizing the reduced map of the detected exterior fermionic mode into a mode-preparation channel and a Hawking thermal channel. At fixed right-left Unruh-mode composition, we then solve a global constrained quantum-channel optimization over all two-qubit resource states whose fully entangled fraction remains at or below the standard teleportation threshold immediately before thermal mixing. A parity twirl and positivity reduce the arbitrary-state problem exactly to a two-variable quadratic optimization. The solution yields a necessary-and-sufficient activation boundary, a second exact boundary for attaining the universal optimum, and explicit optimizing states. The resulting phase diagram contains a strict no-go region, a composition-limited activation region, and a universal-bound region. The analysis converts state-specific observations of Hawking-assisted teleportation into exact channel-level bounds over the full two-qubit state space.

title: Chiral edge modes from lattice Chern-Simons theory
summary: It is shown that a level $k$ Abelian lattice Chern-Simons theory with continuum time and a spatial square lattice, which is a topological field theory on the latticized plane and torus, when quantized on a spatial cylinder reduces to chiral edge excitations, exactly localized on the two boundaries and carrying two commuting lattice versions of the level-$k$ $U(1)$ Kac-Moody algebra of opposite chirality. The algebras are represented on a Fock space in the noncompact theory and by a finite Weyl algebra in the compact one. We also observe that the theory has a natural framing of Wilson loops which exhibits the correct framing anomaly.

title: Low cross-plane thermal conductivity of $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ thin films
summary: The thermal conductivities of (001) $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ thin films deposited on $c$-plane sapphire substrates were measured with frequency-domain thermoreflectance (FDTR). The thermal conductivity increases from 1.83 $^{+0.19}_{-0.18}$ W/m$\cdot$K to 2.26 $^{+0.35}_{-0.40}$ W/m$\cdot$K as the thicknesses increase from 159 nm to 689 nm. This weak thickness dependence indicates that the majority of the intrinsic phonon mean free paths are smaller than the range of investigated film thicknesses. First-principles-based calculations that include phonon-phonon and phonon-boundary scattering capture this size-dependent behavior and support our experimental observation. Temperature-dependent measurements of a 689 nm film from 293 to 400 K show a decrease in thermal conductivity with increasing temperature due to enhanced phonon-phonon scattering. A weaker temperature dependence is observed in a 159 nm film where phonon-boundary scattering becomes more prominent. At comparable film thicknesses, our measured $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ films exhibit lower values of cross-plane thermal conductivity than the other experimentally measured Ga$_2$O$_3$ polymorphs. Our experimental observations are supported by prior predictions, which suggest that the low thermal conductivity of $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ results from its complex crystal structure, which leads to increased anharmonicity and lower phonon group velocities relative to other polymorphs. Thermal management strategies, such as integration with high-thermal-conductivity substrates, may thus be required to mitigate self-heating for $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$-based electronic devices.

title: CMS ECAL Phase-2 upgrade: characterisation and stability analysis of a three-stage low-voltage power-conversion system
comment: 7 pages, 6 figures. Proceedings of the Topical Workshop on Electronics for Particle Physics (TWEPP 2026), 28 September - 2 October 2026, Castelldefels, Spain. Submitted to JINST
summary: As part of the High-Luminosity upgrade of the Large Hadron Collider, the front-end electronics of the Compact Muon Solenoid electromagnetic calorimeter barrel are being replaced. A three-stage low-voltage power-conversion system supplies the upgraded electronics. As the cascade dynamics require characterisation to ensure stable operation, interactions between the three converter stages are assessed at their two interfaces using the Nyquist criterion. A validated shunt-injection setup using a Bode 100 frequency-response analyser provides in-situ impedance measurements under load to assess the accuracy of the averaged converter models. Results show that both interfaces are stable over the evaluated configurations, with modelled minimum distances to the critical point of 0.76 and 0.79, respectively. A turn-on study identifies capacitor charging at Stage 3 as the main cause of inrush currents triggering Stage 2 overcurrent protection. Two Stage 3 board variants stagger converter enables within and between boards, keeping the measured two-tower current below 5 A, within the 8.0 A protection threshold.

title: Compatible Condensation and Generalized Gauging: Marked Transport and Wall Interchange
summary: We formulate condensation compatible with a specified separable generalized gauging operation in a unitary (2 + 1)-dimensional defect realization. Compatibility is a coherent reversible crossing of the full condensate algebra, retaining charged channels and the marked condensation interface. The resulting composite network determines the transported condensate, the induced operation, and a commuting square of specified walls. For connected gauging data, compatibility admits a central matching description that retains the transported condensate and its algebra identification on the specified wall. The specified unit may absorb a nontrivial parent anyon algebra; strong connectedness appears only as the transparent-unit specialization. We distinguish original vacuum insertions, vacuum branches after unit absorption, and the full vacuum algebra of the final phase, and we prove a complete Higgs criterion that incorporates the parent algebra absorbed by the specified unit. In the toric-code example of a non-invertible subgroup gauging we classify the compatible condensations for the fixed operation, exhibit two inequivalent crossings of the same parent condensate that lead to different final phases, and analyse a pure condensation operation in which the specified unit absorbs the parent electric condensate and produces additional final vacuum operators. The transparent-unit case recovers reverse-condensation transport and the vacuum-overlap formula, and the three complete Higgs conditions appear as a corollary of the general criterion.

title: Spacetime Evolution Induced by a Massive Cosmic String in Numerical Relativity
summary: Cosmic strings are one-dimensional topological defects formed during phase transitions in the early universe. ''Massive'' cosmic strings possess a sufficiently large tension to close their transverse space, forming a conical singularity outside the string, as a static gravitational effect. In a dynamical context, such strings are expected to drive topological inflation. In this work, we investigate the spacetime evolution induced by the formation of a massive cosmic string in a radiation-dominated cosmological background, imposing cylindrical symmetry. Using full numerical relativity simulations, we observe that the string core undergoes topological inflation and that its boundary moves inwards superluminally, which causally disconnects the core from the outer universe. Between the core and the asymptotic regions, a nearly matter-dominated decelerating region originates sourced by the oscillating string fields. This region is bounded by a local maximum (''belly'') and local minimum (''throat'') of the circumferential radius, while the throat recedes outwards at about 10% the speed of light. Furthermore, a gravitational wavefront is emitted from the string, characterizing the light cone of the string formation. Even behind the wavefront, the exterior region no longer exhibits a ''conical'' structure. Based on the simulation results, we construct a Penrose diagram, reflecting the causal structure of the entire spacetime.

title: Static and dynamical Casimir effects in a wedge within the worldline formulation
summary: We study a real massless scalar field in $d+1$ dimensions confined to a wedge of opening angle $α$, in the presence of a semitransparent circular arc that may oscillate radially. Within the worldline formulation, and for an arbitrary strength $λ$ of the $δ$-potential that models the arc, we expand the effective action in powers of the radial displacement $R$ of the arc. In this formulation, all the information about the media is contained in the propagator of a non-relativistic point particle, so that known results for that propagator can be used directly. At zeroth order we obtain the Casimir energy of the wedge, with Dirichlet, Neumann or mixed walls, and the contribution of the arc in closed form for arbitrary $λ$. We show that the worldline integrand is, point by point, the energy density obtained from the energy-momentum tensor of the scalar field with curvature coupling $ξ=1/4$; with this identification, and using dimensional regularization for the integrated quantities, we recover the known results for the wedge and for the wedge closed by a Dirichlet arc. At second order in $R$, we reduce the form factor that determines the imaginary part of the in-out effective action, and hence the probability of pair creation by the moving arc, to a one-loop expression involving the radial Green's functions of each angular sector. In the narrow-wedge limit, each angular sector behaves as a field with a mass set by the angular quantization, coupled to a moving $δ$-mirror; for a Dirichlet arc, the pair creation spectrum of the exterior region approaches that of a planar massive mirror, while the interior region behaves as a tapered cavity. Finally, by decomposing the electromagnetic field into TE and TM scalars, we obtain the Casimir energy of wedges with perfectly conducting, perfectly permeable and mixed walls.

title: DefectSkills: Guiding AI agents through first-principles calculations for point defects in semiconductors and insulators
summary: First-principles defect calculations can now be performed autonomously by AI agents, enabled by established computational methods and open-source Python toolkits. However, reliable and repeatable defect calculations require clear scientific and technical guidance that helps agents resolve ambiguities and avoid errors in calculation setup, execution, postprocessing, and analysis. Here, we present DefectSkills, a set of structured prompts that provides human-in-the-loop guidance to AI agents performing first-principles calculations of point defects in semiconductors and insulators using the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP). The prompts encode human expertise and guide agents through unit-cell relaxation, electronic-structure and dielectric calculations, phase-stability and chemical-potential analysis, charged-defect supercell generation and calculations, finite-size corrections, formation-energy calculations and thermodynamic analysis, and data backup. By packaging this expertise as reusable agent skills, DefectSkills supports consistent workflow execution across agentic AI systems and reproducible defect calculations.

title: Cross-Moment Consistency and the Fifth Adler Coefficient in Hadronic Tau Decays
summary: The unknown coefficient $c_{5,1}$ controls the first omitted fifth-order term in fixed-order analyses of inclusive hadronic $τ$ decays. We determine what the four known Adler coefficients can actually test. For any normalized polynomial weight, the fixed-order Adler-to-moment map is triangular with unit diagonal. Hence one common Adler-coefficient error reaches every moment with the same absolute size, and a multi-weight relative test reduces to one absolute tolerance. For three representative weights, a ten-percent test resolves $c_{5,1}$ only to about $\pm24$; the closest contour-improved test is weaker by more than an order of magnitude. Moreover, any continuation that preserves the observed sign of the direct Padé/Shanks defects gives $c_{5,1}\geq378.03$, so values near $280$ require additional structure. A calibration-and-falsification protocol applied to a simplified Beneke--Jamin-type pure-power ansatz gives the conditional estimate $c_{5,1}=248\pm30\,(\mathrm{struct})\pm74\,(\mathrm{method})=248\pm80$. At the physical order its central value coincides algebraically with the exact four-parameter fit; the protocol adds a falsifiable admissibility test and a method uncertainty, not new coefficient information. We also clarify that the often-quoted Beneke--Jamin value $283$ is a linear extrapolation of total-width FOPT te

title: The Quantum Stochastic Limit for Non-Markovian Driving Processes
summary: We express the stochastic limit (weak-coupling limit) of a quantum system interacting with its environment as the limit of solutions to a parametrized family of quantum stochastic differential equations (QSDEs). We prove the convergence of such solutions in the case where the driving processes may be non-Markovian and the system may be infinite-dimensional with unbounded Hamiltonian. We achieve this by imposing a particular condition on the n-point functions of the driving process which we verify for annihilation, creation, and gauge operators on a bosonic Fock space with sufficient mixing. Additionally, we include not only the usual fast-evolving system Hamiltonian which is averaged out in the limit, but also a slow-evolving system Hamiltonian which survives the limit. We also relax the requirement for the fast-evolving Hamiltonian to have a purely discrete spectrum allowing accumulation points under some circumstances. Moreover, our convergence mode for the processes is convergence of all time-centered n-point functions which is stronger than the typical semigroup convergence for the stochastic limit.

title: Research on gravitational waves from extreme mass ratio inspirals in an axisymmetric Finslerian extension of Schwarzschild spacetime
summary: We investigate gravitational waves from extreme mass ratio inspirals in an axisymmetric Finslerian extension of the Schwarzschild spacetime. Its angular component is described by a two-dimensional Randers space, with the Schwarzschild limit recovered at Finslerian parameter $ε= 0$. This structure breaks spherical symmetry, causing generic orbits to undergo orbital plane precession. Using multipolar radiation reaction and adiabatic orbital averaging, we derive the leading order Finslerian corrections to the energy, axial angular momentum, and total angular momentum fluxes. These corrections enter at Newtonian order and take different forms. We then incorporate these corrections into a higher-order Schwarzschild hybrid flux model to evolve the orbital elements and construct waveforms at mass quadrupole order using the numerical kludge method. The Finslerian corrections affect both the conservative orbital dynamics and the dissipative inspiral, producing cumulative phase shifts relative to the Schwarzschild waveform. For the representative source observed by LISA over one year with signal-to-noise ratio of 20, the noise weighted mismatch analysis shows that Finslerian waveforms with $|ε| \gtrsim 2 \times 10^{-6}$ are distinguishable from their Schwarzschild counterparts, with higher initial eccentricities further lowering the distinguishable value of $|ε|$. For a Schwarzschild injection, the Fisher matrix analysis yields a marginalized $1σ$ uncertainty of $σ_ε\simeq 1.26 \times 10^{-6}$. These results show the potential of space-based gravitational wave detectors to probe the axisymmetric Finslerian extension of the Schwarzschild spacetime.

title: Partially Massless Condensates and Reentrant NUT/Bolt Phase Transitions in Conformal Gravity
summary: We study non-Einstein Bach-flat Taub-NUT/Bolt instantons with weakened AdS boundary conditions. In particular, the next-to-leading-order coefficient in the Fefferman--Graham expansion is nonvanishing, and it sources the partially massless response in the dual conformal field theory. As in the Einstein case, the holographic stress tensor of these instantons represents a perfect fluid with vorticity. Remarkably, we identify a non-Einstein Taub-Bolt branch supporting a nonvanishing partially massless response at zero source, while preserving the full symmetry of the squashed conformal boundary. The additional holographic degrees of freedom enrich the thermodynamic phase structure, allowing the conventional NUT/Bolt transition to disappear or give way to reentrant transitions. We further show that non-Einstein Bolts can possess negative thermodynamic volume and establish the absence of negative modes of a conformally coupled probe scalar on regular Bach-flat NUT backgrounds.

title: Medial Model of Elastic Curve Contacts, from Clasps to Knits
comment: 17 pages, 8 figures, submitted as conference proceedings
summary: Materials constructed from interlocking and tangled fibers are challenging to model and understand due in part to the complex interplay between fiber shape and contact mechanics. Much of our intuition about contact mechanics comes from the Hertzian description, which is based on interactions between convex bodies. However, fibers often form clasp shapes, which involve saddle-shaped contact surfaces; the ability for two interacting bodies to conform to each other along a saddle surface confounds many existing mechanical contact models. Following an observation that contact surfaces between fibers tend to look like minimal, constant mean-curvature surfaces, we seek to test this hypothesis and provide a direct link to geometric modeling methods. To do this, we leverage the medial axis transformation, which generalizes the notion of a Voronoi tessellation to generating curves and surfaces. Through computational studies on an orthogonal clasp and a simple knit structure, we find that the medial axis transformation provides a reasonable model for contact surfaces between identical curves. We also show that a generalization of the medial axis transformation based on radical Voronoi tessellations can be used to well-approximate contact surfaces between non-identical curves. We apply this ``radical axis transform'' to curves of different radii and demonstrate a trend for surfaces to adopt finite mean curvature. Our results may point the way towards more sophisticated geometric methods for modeling tangles.

title: Fluctuating Hydrodynamics of Quantum Fluids from the Nonlinear Fokker-Planck Equation
summary: Starting from the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation (NFPE), we establish the fluctuating hydrodynamics for quantum fluids. We also investigate the corresponding stochastic thermodynamics and derive the associated fluctuation theorems. We then apply this framework to both fermionic and bosonic systems. For the ideal Fermi gas, we study the electrical conduction and reveal a resistance proportional to the product of temperature and the density of states at the Fermi surface. For bosonic fluids, we analyze the relaxation time characterizing the critical slowing down phenomenon and identify three distinct scaling behaviors corresponding to the non-interacting, repulsive interaction, and attractive interaction regimes. Overall, this work provides a experimentally verifiable phenomenological description for the dynamics of quantum fluids and demonstrates the applicability of the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation in characterizing such systems.

title: Topology change and the Gauss Bonnet term in causal set theory: the sign of the cosmological term and the axion decay constant
summary: Causal set theory permits changes of spatial topology without the metric degeneracy that forbids them in continuum Lorentzian gravity. In four dimensions such changes enter the gravitational action only through the Gauss--Bonnet term, which is the Euler density. We show that the Euler density of a discrete space is exact, local and combinatorial: it sums to the Euler characteristic at any resolution and is supported on topological defects. The Gauss--Bonnet term of a causal set is therefore fixed rather than postulated. Because it is linear in the number of elements, which is the four-volume, it acts as a cosmological constant. Its coefficient follows without forming any functional derivative, so the known obstruction in the continuum does not arise. The everpresent cosmological constant of causal set theory assumes that the mean topological charge vanishes. We show that it does not. The species of opposite sign solves the field equations only if a positive cosmological constant is already present, and, being simply connected, it cannot carry the axion charge that supports the other species. Only one sign survives, and the sign of the cosmological term is derived rather than assumed. We recover the surviving transition from the causal order alone in every simulated sprinkling. The action of the corresponding axion wormhole then fixes the magnitude. The observed value requires an axion decay constant near the grand unification scale, and this result is insensitive to the one-loop prefactor and to the Gauss--Bonnet coupling.

title: Gluon and Faddeev--Popov ghost propagators in rotating background: An eigenfunction approach
summary: We construct the free gluon and Faddeev--Popov ghost propagators in rigidly rotating cylindrical coordinates using an eigenfunction approach within the Feynman gauge. Starting from the quadratic gauge-fixed QCD action, we derive the corresponding kinetic operators and obtain their spectral representations. For the gluon field, a circular polarization basis diagonalizes the vector wave operator, leading to polarization-dependent shifts in the orders of the radial Bessel functions. In the absence of radial boundaries, we explicitly recover the standard Minkowski propagator in inertial Cartesian coordinates, showing that the off-diagonal tensor components in the cylindrical basis have a geometrical origin. We then extend the construction to a finite-radius cylinder satisfying the causality condition $|Ω|R<1$, imposing relative boundary conditions on the gluon field and Dirichlet conditions on the ghosts. The resulting discrete transverse spectra involve both Dirichlet and Neumann eigenvalues for the gluon modes, from which we obtain explicit spectral representations of the propagators. Our results provide a consistent framework for perturbative QCD calculations in rotating geometries, retaining the angular-momentum, polarization, and boundary effects relevant to future studies of correlation functions and radiative corrections.

title: Ni ordering in the van der Waals gap of Ni-intercalated 2H-NbS$_2$: from disorder through $2\times2$ and $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order to stripe order
comment: 11 Pages 6 figues in main text, 8 pages and 5 figues in supporting material
summary: We report a synchrotron x-ray diffraction study of Ni-intercalated 2H-NbS$_2$ over the range $0.18 \le x \le 0.57$, with Ni contents measured by energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy. Powder diffraction on the whole series shows that the NbS$_2$ host is preserved, while the Ni ions in the van der Waals gap evolve from a disordered arrangement to $2\times2$ order at $x=1/4$ and $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order at $x=1/3$, through a range where both motifs coexist, to an orthorhombic stripe-type order at $x=0.57$. The in-plane lattice parameter increases with Ni content, whereas the interlayer spacing remains nearly constant except for a pronounced minimum at $x=1/4$, which density-functional calculations reproduce for the ordered structure. Single-crystal diffraction on the two commensurate phases shows that the $x=1/4$ structure, with Ni on a single site and a trimerized Nb lattice, is free of stacking faults, whereas the chiral $x=1/3$ structure contains Ni on the nominally empty site, inversion twins and stacking faults of the Ni layers. The comparison between powders and crystals shows that grinding mainly degrades the stacking of the Ni layers. These results establish the structural phase diagram of Ni$_x$NbS$_2$ and the intercalant disorder to be taken into account in the interpretation of its magnetic properties.

title: Spectral properties of twisted soft waveguides
summary: We discuss a model of a soft waveguide described by Schrödinger operator whose potential is a twisted straight channel of non-circular profile. We show that a compactly supported twist makes the operator subcritical, the property being expressed in terms of a Hardy-type inequality. On the other hand, a periodic twist raises the essential spectrum and its local slowdown may give rise to isolated eigenvalues below the essential spectrum threshold.

title: Coupled membrane response and horizon dissipation in four-dimensional Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
summary: We develop an action-based membrane paradigm for nonextremal, static, spherically symmetric black holes in four-dimensional Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet (EsGB) gravity, describing their interaction with external perturbations through an effective fluid membrane. We calculate the linear membrane responses to perturbations and use them to analyze the work done on the membrane and the energy absorbed by the horizon. Horizon energy absorption receives contributions from geometric shear and scalar interactions. The scalar contribution includes both direct work on the membrane and work associated with the induced horizon expansion. We then establish a balance relation between the integrated horizon absorption and the second-order change in Wald entropy between stationary horizon cuts. Applying this framework to slow dynamics near a simple turning point, we obtain the leading exponential growth or decay rate of spherically symmetric scalar perturbations without fitting a dynamical damping coefficient.

title: On phases of 4d $Spin/SO$ Yang-Mills theories
summary: We study the low-temperature phase diagrams of $Spin(N)/SO(N)_\pm$ Yang-Mills theories as functions of the $θ$-parameter. In particular, for every even integer $N\geq 4$, we find a phase diagram consistent with the center/CP mixed anomaly, via the technique of mixed gauge theory. The resulting phase diagrams are in perfect agreement with the phase diagrams of $Spin(N)/SO(N)_\pm$ super Yang-Mills theory softly broken by a small gaugino mass. In the case of $Spin(4k)$ Yang-Mills for an integer $k\geq 2$, only two phases appear in the phase diagram, while in the $Spin(4)$ case the phase diagram contains four SPT phases protected by the $\mathbb{Z}_2\times \mathbb{Z}_2$ center symmetry. In the case of $Spin(4k+2)$ Yang-Mills for a positive integer $k$, the phase diagram contains four SPT phases protected by the $\mathbb{Z}_4$ center symmetry.

title: Exact Mirror-Parity Selection Rule for Electron-Phonon Coupling in Two-Dimensional Crystals
summary: The electron--phonon (e-ph) interaction underlies conventional superconductivity and plays a central role in transport and other many-body phenomena in solids. Here, we derive a symmetry selection rule for e-ph scattering in two-dimensional crystals possessing a horizontal mirror plane, $σ_h$. For electronic states of mirror parity $s_n(\mathbf{k})$ and $s_m(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q})$, and a phonon mode of parity $χ_ν(\mathbf{q})$, we show that the e-ph matrix element $g_{mn,ν}(\mathbf{k},\mathbf{q})$ vanishes identically unless $s_n(\mathbf{k})\,χ_ν(\mathbf{q})\, s_m(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q})=+1$. The rule follows from the covariance of the phonon-induced deformation potential under $σ_h$, constitutes the $C_s$ case of the general group-theoretical selection rule for matrix elements, and partitions the e-ph interaction throughout the Brillouin zone into symmetry-allowed and symmetry-forbidden scattering channels. Consequently, mirror-even phonons couple electronic states of the same mirror parity, either even--even or odd--odd, whereas mirror-odd phonons couple only states of opposite mirror parity, for both intra- and interband processes. We illustrate the selection rule through first-principles calculations for the two-dimensional superconductor $\mathrm{Sc_2BCH_4}$, where mirror parity is well defined throughout the entire Brillouin zone and symmetry-forbidden matrix elements vanish up to numerical precision. We then extend the analysis to bulk $\mathrm{MgB_2}$, where the rule applies exactly only on mirror-invariant planes of the three-dimensional Brillouin zone. Moving away from these planes removes the exact mirror constraint and activates scattering channels that are symmetry forbidden when the mirror eigenvalues are well defined. Our results establish horizontal mirror symmetry as an exact and practical filter of e-ph scattering processes.

title: A Counterexample to the Weak Gibbs and Regularity Conjectures
summary: We provide a counterexample to the weak Gibbs and regularity conjectures. The example is a spin-one system on the square lattice with a translation-invariant nearest-neighbor interaction. At high temperatures and high on-site field strengths, it has a unique KMS state that does not have the weak Gibbs or regularity properties.

title: Missing solutions in scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
summary: We discover novel neutron star solutions under scalar-Gauss-Bonnet (sGB) gravity which have been missed altogether in the existing literature. The complete solution space also reveals a new regularity condition that has to be satisfied by all scalarized stars. Certain scalarized branches of neutron star solutions under sGB gravity have long been known to abruptly terminate on stellar mass-radius diagrams at lower stellar radii, a phenomenon that has no counterpart in classical scalar-tensor theories. Such termination has been strongly suspected to be physical rather than a numerical artifact nevertheless, since sGB theories feature a regularity condition at the center of the star, which can prevent the existence of certain configurations. Motivated by the recently re-emerging phase-transition view of scalarization, we first predict that these terminated branches can reappear after a "gap." We confirm this by finding such reappearing branches, and also determine which parts of the theory parameter space are more amenable to such occurrences. We then show that the previously known central regularity condition cannot explain all the non-existing solutions in the gaps, which leads us to the discovery of a new, non-central, condition for the existence of scalarized neutron stars under sGB gravity.

title: Spectral flow in AdS$\mathbf{_3}$ revisited
comment: 66 pages, 6 figures. Includes ancillary Mathematica notebook
summary: We revisit an old idea that spectral flow in WZW models can be associated with certain $G$-bundles over a worldsheet. This allows us to introduce a novel method for computing correlators of spectrally-flowed vertex operators in WZW models with group $G$ and level $k$, by systematically computing the contribution from a network of line defects. Specialising to the case of $G=SL(2, \mathbb{R})$, as is relevant to AdS$_3$ string theory, we demonstrate that generic $n$-point functions of spectrally-flowed vertex operators at tree level can be rewritten in terms of an $(n+1)$-point function of $n$ unflowed vertex operators and one degenerate insertion. This is to be interpreted as an unflowed $n$-point function in an instanton background. Moreover, we conjecture that this $(n+1)$-point function can be recast as an $n$-point function of unflowed operators and we provide evidence for this. We demonstrate that the $(n+1)$-point function satisfies the same constraints from global spacetime conformal invariance as does an unflowed $n$-point function for a specific choice of spacetime coordinates that we determine. We verify that our results agree with bootstrap results in the literature. This provides the next step towards fully solving the $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ WZW model.

authors: Pieter Hendrik Willem Van Der Hoek
title: Topological localization in unentangled random braids
comment: 22 pages, 12 figures, separated gif-files with animations
summary: In 2015, P. Serna, G. Bunin, and A. Nahum numerically investigated fluctuations in a bunch of unentangled random threads. They showed that fluctuations of an individual thread in a braid are qualitatively different from those of a thread embedded in a medium of fixed parallel lines. In particular, Serna et al. observed a logarithmic increase in the average transverse span, $\left<|x_N|\right>$, of a thread with polymer length, $N$. This behavior highlights the collective nature of topological interactions, in which each polymer fluctuates and constrains the motion of the others. Studying this problem both numerically and analytically, we propose the following interpretation: the logarithmic regime is transient, and sufficiently long polymers exhibit topological localization, where $\left<|x_N|\right>$ approaches a finite limit at $N\to\infty$. Unlike localization induced by quenched external disorder, this phenomenon arises solely from collective topological constraints. We study braids within a locally free approximation and support the localization by analytical investigation of Brownian bridges on the asymptotic Cayley graph of a locally free group. We further conjecture that topologically induced localization emerges as a phase transition: for a small number of threads, $n \sim 2÷5$, the span, $\left<|x_N|\right>$, grows algebraically, with the usual scaling $\left<|x_N|\right>\sim N^{1/4}$ at $N\gg 1$; by contrast, for sufficiently large $n$, each thread in a long braid ($N\gg 1$) asymptotically localizes, approaching $\left<|x_N|\right>\sim \mathrm{const}$.

title: Large particle number asymptotics for point-interacting bosons in the plane
summary: We consider $N$ bosons in two dimensions interacting via point interactions, modeled by the TMS Hamiltonian. We prove that their ground state energy has the asymptotic behavior $-e^{C N }$ for large $N$, for an explicit constant $C$ related to the sharp constant in the Ladyzhenskaya-Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. Such asymptotic behavior was predicted in the physics literature, based on a variant of the mean-field approximation.

title: Metric reconstruction in a Bondi-like gauge
summary: Metric perturbations obtained from a Hertz potential in an ingoing radiation gauge (IRG) generically grow in an outgoing coordinate $r$ at future null infinity, and are therefore not asymptotically flat in the Bondi sense. Hollands and Toomani showed that this growth can be removed, within the Green--Hollands--Zimmerman (GHZ) framework, by an IRG-compatible ``residual'' gauge transformation together with a carefully chosen choice of the undetermined integration ``constants'' of the Hertz potential. In this work we turn that proof into a practical algorithm. We show that this entire completion is generated by a single ``Held Master Scalar'' (HMS), which can be thought of as a function on future null infinity. The HMS is obtained from the leading asymptotic piece of the $0$-Weyl scalar through a Teukolsky--Starobinsky inversion. We give explicit formulas for the four integration constants of the Hertz potential associated with the $0$-Weyl scalar, and for the residual gauge vector in terms of the HMS, thereby bringing the metric perturbation into a Bondi-like gauge. In Schwarzschild the entire construction is diagonal in $(\ell, m)$-modes and every completion field is available in closed form; in Kerr the construction is tri-diagonal. We have numerically implemented the full scheme in $(\ell,m)$ and in $m$-modes, including the corrector piece of the GHZ framework. We illustrate our scheme numerically for a point-particle on a circular orbit in a puncture scheme in Schwarzschild and in Kerr, by demonstrating the Bondi-like fall-off. We also find agreement with the known Detweiler redshift computations in Schwarzschild and Kerr. Our method directly gives the Bondi news, mass-, and angular momentum aspects, for which we give exemplary results in Kerr.

title: A dynamical Einstein-Proca-dilaton holographic model and exotic hybrid meson resonances
summary: A fully dynamical Einstein-Proca-dilaton (EPD) holographic model is developed for the exotic $J^{PC}=1^{-+}$ hybrid meson, incorporating the backreaction of the massive vector field dual to the hybrid current in the bulk. Solving the coupled EPD system yields a self-consistent gravitational background and the mass spectrum of hybrid resonances. While the soft-wall limit reproduces linear Regge behavior, the inclusion of backreaction yields quantitative shifts that improve agreement with experimental candidates. The finite-temperature regime is approached by studying black hole thermodynamics and spectral functions across the confinement-deconfinement transition, fixing the Hawking-Page temperature to $T_c \sim 150 \, \mathrm{MeV}$. Unlike non-backreacted AdS/QCD models, the dynamical background predicts a strong suppression of hybrid states already near the onset of deconfinement. These results demonstrate that gravitational backreaction has measurable consequences for both vacuum spectroscopy and in-medium properties of exotic hybrid mesons, emphasizing the relevance of a dynamical self-consistent approach in AdS/QCD.

title: Shock-driven Jetting at HMX Crystal Surface Asperities
summary: Shock-induced jetting and recompression are plausible mechanisms for hot spot formation in energetic materials, but remain poorly understood. To this end, we apply all-atom nonreactive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of a shock-loaded sinusoidal surface asperity in the crystalline explosive HMX (octahydro-1,3,5,7-tetranitro-1,3,5,7-tetrazocine) to quantify the roles of shock strength, asperity geometry, system size, and crystallographic orientation in determining the jetting response. Our simulations span a shock pressure interval of $\approx$4-47 GPa, which captures responses in both detonation initiation and steady-state detonation regimes. We find that shock strength and asperity curvature exert strong influence on jet velocity, temperature, and morphology, while feature size and crystallographic orientation play more modest roles. Jet morphology correlates strongly with the HMX ambient-pressure phase diagram and the narrow temperature range associated with its liquid phase. Coherent jets form when focusing and dissipation are sufficient to drive local temperatures above the melting point, while formation of molecular plumes is seemingly connected to jet temperatures exceeding the liquid-vapor transition temperature. Formation of plumes is unlike the jetting responses seen in metals, which typically exhibit liquid phases that are stable over wider temperature intervals. This work proposes a simple hypothesis for the connection between jet morphology and ambient-pressure phase diagrams that can be readily tested in other explosives and metals. It also provides a foundation for ongoing nonreactive and reactive MD simulations of jet impact and recompression to quantify the role played by jets in forming hot spots in HMX-based explosives.

title: Concavity of Normalized Generalized Brézin--Gross--Witten Correlators and Its Applications
summary: In this paper, we study the generalized Brézin--Gross--Witten model using its BKP integrability. By virtue of the formula for connected $n$-point functions of tau-functions of the BKP hierarchy obtained by Wang and the first-named author, we prove that the normalized generalized BGW correlators are strictly concave for fixed genus and fixed total degree. As applications, we establish the strict Schur-concavity and derive upper and lower bounds for these correlators. We also prove the strict monotonicity of normalized ordinary BGW correlators, which resolves a conjecture by Guo--Norbury--Yang--Zagier.

title: Constraining Lorentz Invariance Violation via Precision Atomic Spectroscopy
summary: This paper investigates Lorentz violation arising from quantum gravity effects in electronic and muonic hydrogen atoms. The violation is modeled through a modified dispersion relation parameterized by a dimensionless coefficient $ξ$ and suppressed by the Planck scale. Using high-precision spectroscopic data and a chi-squared fitting procedure that carefully accounts for theoretical uncertainties in the Rydberg constant and the proton radius, the analysis yields a 95% confidence level constraint $ξ\in [-14.3,\; 1.37] \times 10^5$. The mass scaling of the effect reveals two distinct regimes: for the lowest-order deformation, the heavy nucleus amplifies the signal, while for higher-order corrections, the lepton dominates the sensitivity.
